title: Routing policy audit and corrective actions after incorrect variant fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: During a cross-region capacity event on 2025-02-14, the smart routing layer performed fallbacks to model variants that were incompatible with the requesting tenant's pinned constraints, causing a ~7 minute outage for a subset of production traffic. This issue manifested as hundreds of 5xx errors and elevated latencies for customers on Dedicated plans.

Timeline:
- 2025-02-14 02:03 UTC: Autoscaling pressure in eu-west-1 started causing model variant pool depletion.
- 2025-02-14 02:08 UTC: Smart routing attempted fallback to nearest compatible region; policy allowed variant substitution that violated tenant pin constraint and resulted in variant mismatch errors.
- 2025-02-14 02:09–02:16 UTC: Re-route loop observed for small percentage of traffic as routing policy retried incompatible variants.
- 2025-02-14 02:17 UTC: Automated circuit-breaker tripped, traffic degraded to error pages for affected customers.
- 2025-02-14 02:22 UTC: Emergency mitigation: restrict fallback to explicit compatible variant set, manually unblock pinned tenants.
- 2025-02-14 03:05 UTC: Normal routing restored.

This ticket captures the audit findings from the incident, the agreed root cause, and the list of follow-up remediations with owners and dates.
postmortem_summary:
Root cause: routing policy evaluation permitted fallback substitutions that did not respect tenant-level model pin constraints when a variant pool was empty. A secondary contributing factor was a logic bug in cross-region compatibility matching that returned stale compatibility metadata after a rolling upgrade.

Impact: ~7 minutes of elevated errors for Dedicated tenants depending on eu-west-1 capacity; some requests retried in loops leading to cascading load and increased tail latency in adjacent regions.

Resolution: Immediate mitigation tightened fallback policy to require explicit compatibility confirmation and enabled a fast rollback path to the original region for pinned tenants. A code patch to fail fast on incompatible fallback was deployed in routing-2025.02 emergency patch.
root_cause: Policy layer allowed implicit variant substitution when local capacity was exhausted. The substitution check used out-of-date compatibility cache and did not check tenant pin metadata atomically with the routing decision. Additionally, circuit-breaker thresholds did not account for retry storms in multi-region reroute scenarios.
remediation_plan: RP-1: Add atomic tenant-pin + variant compatibility check in routing decision path | owner: Evelyn Park | ETA: 2025-02-28 | status: Done
RP-2: Implement TTL and validation for compatibility metadata cache; invalidate on model rollouts | owner: Marcelo Ruiz | ETA: 2025-03-07 | status: In Progress
RP-3: Introduce 'safe-fallback' mode that only considers variants explicitly marked compatible by model-onboarding metadata | owner: Sanaa Iqbal | ETA: 2025-03-12 | status: In Progress
RP-4: Update circuit-breaker logic to recognize multi-region retry storms and throttle retry fanout | owner: Rajesh Patel | ETA: 2025-03-10 | status: In Progress
RP-5: Add end-to-end integration tests simulating capacity exhaustion + pinned-tenants to CI gating for routing changes | owner: Test Infra | ETA: 2025-03-05 | status: In Review
RP-6: Run a scheduled audit of tenants with pinned models and add monitoring alert when pinned variant becomes unavailable | owner: Platform SRE | ETA: 2025-03-01 | status: Done
RP-7: Update runbook and post-incident checklist to include fast-path manual override for pinned tenants | owner: Ops Docs | ETA: 2025-02-25 | status: Done
owners: Evelyn Park - Routing policy change owner
Marcelo Ruiz - Compatibility cache and metadata validation
Sanaa Iqbal - Model onboarding and safe-fallback implementation
Rajesh Patel - Circuit-breaker and retry throttling
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Initial ticket created with audit notes and mitigation recap (Aisha).
2025-02-20: RP-1 deployed to staging and verified with synthetic traffic; staging test passed (Evelyn).
2025-02-22: Emergency patch for fail-fast incompatible fallback deployed to prod; immediate error spike reduced (Release: routing-2025.02).
2025-02-26: Compatibility cache TTL design reviewed with infra; Marcelo to deliver patch by 2025-03-07.
2025-03-01: Monitoring alert for pinned-variant-unavailable firing correctly in prod; Platform SRE confirmed silences and escalations.
2025-03-04: RP-5 tests opened as PR and awaiting test infra sign-off (PR: #4387).
notes: Follow-ups include a post-deployment verification window for routing-2025.03 to validate no regression in variant-safety logic. Recommend a canary rollout to 5% of traffic for the safe-fallback feature with detailed latency and error dashboards. Consider retrofitting older model variants with explicit compatibility tags to prevent future metadata ambiguity.
